name: Chromium
clinical_note: Interpret with clinical context; routine status assessment is limited.

name: Copper
clinical_note: Consider deficiency and excess, particularly with prolonged medical nutrition or altered losses.

name: Fluoride
clinical_note: Provision varies; use the guideline and local formulation information.

name: Iodine
clinical_note: Consider thyroid context and iodine exposure when interpreting status.

name: Iron
clinical_note: Inflammation substantially complicates interpretation of iron biomarkers.

name: Manganese
clinical_note: Toxicity is an important concern in prolonged PN; interpret whole-blood values and clinical context.

name: Molybdenum
clinical_note: Deficiency is uncommon; prolonged nutrition support may justify review.

name: Selenium
clinical_note: Inflammation can alter circulating selenium; interpret alongside CRP.

name: Zinc
clinical_note: Requirements may increase with substantial gastrointestinal, wound, burn, or other losses.

name: Vitamin A
clinical_note: Avoid indiscriminate high-dose supplementation; consider hepatic function and toxicity.

name: Vitamin D
clinical_note: Status is assessed with serum 25(OH)D; deficiency treatment is distinct from routine provision.

name: Vitamin E
clinical_note: Interpret status with lipid concentrations and clinical context.

name: Vitamin K
clinical_note: Consider anticoagulant therapy, cholestasis, malabsorption and prolonged antibiotic exposure.

name: Thiamin (Vitamin B1)
clinical_note: Higher doses are used in selected high-risk states; refeeding-risk management requires separate consideration.

name: Riboflavin (Vitamin B2)
clinical_note: Assessment is not routinely required; consider deficiency risk and prolonged inadequate intake.

name: Niacin (Vitamin B3)
clinical_note: Consider deficiency in prolonged poor intake or malabsorption; pharmacologic dosing is outside routine provision.

name: Pantothenic Acid (Vitamin B5)
clinical_note: Deficiency is uncommon; routine provision differs from treatment of suspected deficiency.

name: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)
clinical_note: Plasma PLP is affected by inflammation; red-cell PLP may be more informative in serious illness.

name: Biotin (Vitamin B7)
clinical_note: Deficiency is uncommon but may occur with severe malnutrition, malabsorption or prolonged nutrition support.

name: Folate (Vitamin B9)
clinical_note: Interpret folate together with vitamin B12 status where clinically relevant.

name: Cobalamin (Vitamin B12)
clinical_note: Serum B12 alone may be insufficient in selected cases; functional biomarkers can support assessment.

name: Vitamin C
clinical_note: Plasma vitamin C is difficult to interpret during critical illness or severe inflammation.
